checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. The 'Legs and feet' checkpoint was correctly marked untestable due to occlusion by grass. The 'Female' checkpoint was correctly marked N/A as the subject is male. The Router correctly identified the presence of red combs, white undertail patch, and black plumage. However, the Router may have been slightly lenient on the 'iridescence' checkpoint; while present, the sheen is somewhat muted compared to high-quality real photographs, but this is acceptable for AI generation at this resolution.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies in the white patch (severity 1.5) and beak blur (severity 1.0). The Perceptual Quality Auditor detected slight compression artifacts (severity 0.2). I agree with these assessments. The Topology Boundary Auditor's high confidence score (0.9894) confirms the bird's outline is coherent and not fragmented. The Geometric Depth Auditor found no grounding issues. There are no catastrophic structural failures. The 'smudged' white feathers are a minor textural artifact common in diffusion models when rendering fine, high-contrast details like white feathers against dark bodies or green backgrounds.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine Grained Classifier strongly confirms the class 'black grouse' (logit 7.78 vs 1.79 for next closest). All visible anatomical checkpoints (combs, beak, body shape, tail flare, white patch) are present and correct. The image aligns very well with the taxonomy prior knowledge for a male blackcock.
artifact_reasoning: Minor textural smoothing in the white undertail coverts and slight beak blur prevent a perfect score. However, the boundary integrity is high (SAM confidence ~0.99), and there is no melting or fusion with the background. The artifacts are subtle and do not detract significantly from the overall realism.
key_defects: Slight painterly/smudged texture in white undertail feathers
